items.title: Hype Reel | DevCon 5
items.hover_description: DevCon 5 was about putting new products and capabilities in the hands of builders. We showed the latest releases — across AI FDE, Orchestrator, Ontology Foundations, the revamped Developer Experience, and more. Then builders got to work.

items.title: Deep Dive: Interoperability at Scale with the Multimodal Data Plane | DevCon 5
items.hover_description: Modularity and interoperability, without compromising on speed or scale. At DevCon 5, Palantir Group Lead Ted Chester Jenks goes deep on the Multimodal Data Plane (MMDP) — the next-generation data and compute architecture that powers Palantir Foundry and AIP. From virtual tables and compute pushdown with external systems, to native Iceberg tables and a new SQL engine for interacting with both tables and the Ontology.

items.title: Product Launch: Hivemind | DevCon 5
items.hover_description: Dynamically generated, Ontology-powered fleets of agents. At DevCon 5, Palantir Product Manager Ben Radford walks through the architecture of AI Hivemind — covering the capabilities and tradecraft that enable the creation, orchestration, and optimization of specialized agent teams.

items.title: Product Launch: Developer Experience | DevCon 5
items.hover_description: Human-agent teaming requires a human-agent developer experience. At DevCon 5, Palantir Group Lead John Ayad offers a first look at the future of pro-code development in Foundry and AIP — introducing a new CLI that enables developers and agents to create pro-code monorepos for end-to-end applications, which include data pipelines, ontology primitives, and application artifacts. Rapid iteration and robust security, for both human and AI developers.

items.title: Product Launch: Ontology Foundations | DevCon 5
items.hover_description: Powerful agents require powerful foundations. At DevCon 5, Palantir Group Lead Kevin Foley and Software Engineer Laura Arias Fernandez walk through the latest Ontology capabilities — voice-integrated agents, what-if scenario modeling for workflow expansion, and granular security controls and atomic transactions for workflow guardrails. The result is agents that are not just capable, but ready for production workflows at scale.

items.title: Product Launch: AI FDE | DevCon 5
items.hover_description: Forward deployed engineering is no longer limited to humans. At DevCon 5, Palantir Software Engineers Ankit Shankar and Colton Rusch demonstrate new AI FDE capabilities to write AIP Logic functions, author evals, and safely debug in a branch-aware, continuous loop. Watch as a manual process is automated live — agents building other agents, and navigating the entire AI engineering lifecycle, from first draft to a production-ready system that gets smarter with every interaction.

items.title: Product Launch: Enterprise Automation | DevCon 5
items.hover_description: Durable, interruptible, long-running agents enable enterprise autonomy. At DevCon 5, AIP Development Lead Matt Hawes and Forward Deployed Engineer Vishesh Patel launch Orchestrator — a a new execution framework for long-running agents and automations. See how Orchestrator and the Ontology come together to enable true human-agent teaming at enterprise scale.

items.title: Akshay Krishnaswamy Opening Remarks | DevCon 5
items.hover_description: “You need maximum leverage to swarm at problems as fast as possible with human-agent teams, to metabolize learnings and iterate on new problems at machine speed, and to fuel a compounding intelligence core that is shared across all the outcomes you're pursuing” Watch as Palantir Chief Architect Akshay Krishnaswamy delivers the opening remarks at DevCon 5.
